round1_to_round2.summary: All five agents made the corrections I asked for in round 1, and most checked them against primary sources themselves rather than copying them. Fair values moved down $1-2 each (from $96-107 to $95-105, mean from $100.4 to $99.2), mostly because of the ~86M diluted share count. The 12-month mean ladder barely moved (P>=107 went from 0.467 to 0.463), and the spread between agents narrowed (at K=107, from 0.055 to 0.035). The 1-month ladders collapsed onto my round-1 ladder: the round-2 mean is within 0.003 of it at every strike.
round1_to_round2.independent_or_anchored: The convergence is mixed. On the earnings date (~Nov 4, outside the 1-month window) it is anchoring on a verified shared fact, which is legitimate: agents 1, 2 and 3 re-checked the EDGAR 8-K cadence, and agents 4 and 5 had called Nov 4-5 independently in round 1. But the 1-month ladders reproduce my round-1 shape almost exactly (three agents adopted a ~0.10-0.102 core sigma with the same 10% wide component), so that agreement is not independent evidence and counts as about one view. On the 12-month view, agents kept their own multiples and thesis breaks and argued against me where they disagreed (agent_2 at $68, agent_3 at $72, agent_4 keeping a $105 fair value, agent_5 keeping its 20% peak-multiple leg). So the 12-month spread is still mostly independent. The clearest sign of anchoring is a shared error: all five still use the '~$11.40 Q1-guide run-rate' that I endorsed in round-1 key_drivers. That figure annualizes a 14-week quarter (see disagreements). None of the five caught it; agent_1 even wrote 'a 14-week quarter' and still used x4.

disagreements.topic: NEW (missed by all five and by me in round 1): the Q1 FY27 guide covers a 14-week quarter, so 'x4 = $11.40 run-rate' overstates annual earnings power
disagreements.positions: All five agents use the $2.85 Q1 guide x 4 = ~$11.40 (agent_5 $11.27 on 86M) as the run-rate, and say consensus (~$10.5) 'lags guidance'. Agents 1, 4 and 5 build FY27/NTM EPS of $11.5-12.4 on it. Agent_3 says the 53rd week is offset by convert dilution.
disagreements.resolution: FY26 ended Jun 27, 2026 and Q1 FY27 ends Oct 3, 2026, which is 98 days, or 14 weeks. The 10-K says fiscal 2027 has 53 weeks. In the identical FY16 calendar, the Q1 10-Q (quarter ended Oct 3, 2015) states that 'the first quarter of fiscal 2016 ... contained 14 weeks' and attributes most y/y growth to the extra week. The 13-week equivalent of the guide is ~$2.65 EPS (somewhat less after operating leverage) and ~$8.5B sales. Underlying sequential growth is then ~+2-3%, not the headline ~10%, and the annualized run-rate is ~$10.4-10.6, in line with the ~$10.5 FY27 consensus. Consensus does not lag the guide. Agents' NTM EPS above ~$11 is overstated by ~5-10%. A second effect: Q2 FY27 (13 weeks) guidance on Nov 4 may look flat or down on Q1 even if demand is still growing. Agents list 'a sequential guide-down' as a thesis-break signal, so it must be judged on a 13-week basis.
disagreements.evidence: FY26 10-K (fiscal 2027 will contain 53 weeks); Q4 FY26 Ex.99.1 (Q1 ends Oct 3, 2026; ~10% sequential growth at the midpoint; the release does not mention the extra week); Q1 FY16 10-Q (14-week quarter ended Oct 3, 2015, 'extra week of sales'); day count Jun 27 to Oct 3 = 98 days.

confidence_reason: I settled with primary filings a factual error that all five shared: the 14-week Q1 makes the '$11.40 run-rate' ~7% too high. It lowers every agent's EPS-based fair value by $3-9. thesis_break_reason: $66 is about -38% and ~6.2x a ~$10.6 13-week-equivalent run-rate, the ~6x multiple Avnet traded at on FY23 peak adjusted EPS of $8.06. Trading there would mean the market has decided the cycle has peaked: book-to-bill below 1, memory price reversal, or customer inventory unwind.
